title: Advanced painting and typography tools
summary: Expand the pixel editor with enhanced fill controls, linear and radial gradients, ordered gradient dithering, and editable text while preserving pixel-precise undoable workflows across desktop and touch devices.

questions.question: What lifecycle makes text genuinely editable after placement?
questions.answer: Go with the recommended live text-layer model.
questions.decision: Placing text creates a dedicated live text layer that remains editable after reopening; export and explicit Rasterize Text convert it to hard pixel output. This keeps ordinary pixel cels clean and makes font fallback, selection, history, and schema migration explicit.

questions.question: Which shape tools share one mode control versus appearing as separate rail items?
questions.decision: Keep Rectangle and Circle/Ellipse as separate tools with one shared Outline/Filled mode and shared thickness settings; do not multiply toolbox entries or shortcuts.

questions.question: What exact Pixel-perfect Freehand cleanup rule should apply at joins and stroke intersections?
questions.decision: Remove only redundant single-pixel corner stair-step artifacts when the neighboring stroke path proves the pixel is a duplicate; preserve intentional isolated pixels and intersections.

questions.question: Which spray distributions and deterministic/repeatable behavior are required?
questions.decision: Ship deterministic seeded uniform scatter by default, plus Gaussian/center-weighted and edge-preserving distributions; replaying the same gesture uses the same seed for stable previews, undo, and tests.

questions.question: Which color-distance model and tolerance scale should Fill use?
questions.decision: Use RGBA-aware weighted color distance with a 0–255 tolerance, 4-way contiguous matching by default, optional 8-way connectivity, and non-contiguous all-matching-pixels mode.

questions.question: What area/selection masking contract applies to gradient and text placement?
questions.decision: An active selection clips gradients and rasterized text; without one, operations clip to the canvas. Text starts at the clicked anchor and never writes outside canvas bounds.

questions.question: Which bundled/system pixel fonts are supported, and what happens when a font is missing?
questions.decision: Bundle OFL-licensed Pixelify Sans and Silkscreen, permit installed system fonts, and show a warning while falling back to a bundled pixel font when a selected font is unavailable.

questions.question: What brush-size and computational ceilings define performance acceptance?
questions.decision: 1000×1000 remains interactive during brush/shape preview without full-project cloning per pointer event; localized strokes target a 16 ms frame budget, full-canvas fill/gradient commits may use a worker or bounded batch up to 100 ms, brush size is capped at 64, and spray radius at 64.

dependencies.reason: The in-progress customizable toolbox owns preference normalization and presentation for new stable tool IDs; implementation can proceed independently but overlapping tool-definition files require coordination.

risks: Full-canvas fill/gradient can freeze phones; cap dimensions/options, reuse buffers, profile 1000×1000 fixtures, and move only measured expensive commits to workers.
Shape thickening can create uneven corners; define integer footprint semantics and golden fixtures at shallow, steep, degenerate, and clipped bounds.
Pixel-perfect cleanup can erase intentional art; use conservative path-provenance checks and an option to disable cleanup per gesture.
Composite fill can accidentally write hidden or inactive layers; separate read buffer from active write target and assert layer IDs in tests.
Text font substitution can change appearance; bundle licensed fallbacks, persist resolved family, warn on substitution, and provide explicit Rasterize Text.
New tools can break customized rails/shortcuts; use stable IDs, preference normalization, and required Pencil/Eraser/Hand invariants.
Touch hover affordances do not exist; provide visible controls, long-press or tap paths, and keyboard alternatives on desktop.
Text-layer rendering may diverge between Canvas2D and exports; use one hard-edge raster helper for preview/export and compare pixel fixtures.
validation: Unit-test brush footprints, pixel-perfect joins, thick lines, outline/filled shape points, contour closure, cancellation, and one-entry undo.

Test deterministic spray, RGBA fill tolerance, connectivity, non-contiguous matching, visible-layer reads, indexed limits, grayscale normalization, gradients, ordered dither, selection masks, and text schema migration.
Playwright-test desktop, tablet, phone, touch cancellation, contextual controls, text editing, missing-font fallback, accessibility, high-resolution interaction, tiled/live previews, and exports.
Profile 1000×1000 interaction budgets and optimize only measured hot paths.
Run affected-file Prettier, studio lint/typecheck/unit/build, focused/full Playwright, root checks, pnpm spec validate TOOLS-C4EX, and git diff --check.
validationEvidence: Studio lint, typecheck, production build, and 78 unit tests pass. Added deterministic raster fixtures and docs/ai/drawing-tools.md. Remaining work: dedicated E2E/performance profiling.

Focused Playwright regression for advanced tools passed on desktop (1 test). Full cross-device E2E and measured 1000x1000 performance profiling remain follow-up work; spec intentionally stays in_progress.
